P1.evidence: The only call in this batch where setter notes existed and were acknowledged - 'I got the notes. From Kyla, I'm clear on that' - but nothing was actually read back, so the prospect got no sense of being seen or pre-understood; it functioned as a throwaway line before the open question. The frame ran the same two of four parts used on every call in this batch: 'go deep on what you've got going on with your fitness right now and also what it is you're looking to accomplish', with nothing on obstacles or needs. Frame agreement was taken and given. Open question asked cleanly.

P2.evidence: The weakest baseline of the batch, on the oldest prospect in it. Age, height and weight were never asked - 47 was volunteered mid-story and drew surprise ('You're 47... I would have guessed, like, 30-some'), and the 10-12% body fat figure was also volunteered. Occupation was volunteered ('for my job, I'm a teacher') and only then followed up, and the rep still had it wrong at the end of the call, calling it a 'gym teacher's salary' after being told twice it was English. Health conditions, injuries, chronic pain and movement limitations were never asked at all - not one question, on a 47-year-old about to be sold loaded ballistic training. Diet was never asked despite nutrition being a third of the offer. Sleep was never asked. Energy was volunteered ('I just have so much more present in the moment focus') and never asked. Training week and current results were genuinely well covered and are the only two clean hits.

P3.evidence: The bridge question was asked properly and was the best moment on the call: 'is there anything else that is going on right now... Is there anything that's really, like, you know, pushing you, I guess, to, to make some changes now?' It produced an honest and important answer - 'I don't think there's any one thing right now that is a major catalyst for me right now' - which the rep correctly identified as the crux and then did nothing with. The deep material was all volunteered and left on the table: a divorce, a five-year reinvention, wanting to sprint in twenty years, wanting a partner who shares the outlook, and children. The children are the clearest omission - the prospect said 'I've got my kids, I'm raising, you know, and, okay, do having to do co-parent thing' and the rep never asked a single question about them, despite P3f and P3g existing precisely for that. The reflect-back at 00:13:30 listed three themes accurately but never converted them into 'so this isn't really about X, it's about Y - is that right?'

P4.evidence: This phase fits the prospect poorly and the rep did not adapt it. What he tried was established - five years of self-taught calisthenics, Spartan race training, a CrossFit-style gym he evaluated and rejected - and what happened with it was covered: it worked. Nothing failed and nothing stopped sticking, by his own account: 'I stayed on the wagon. I didn't fall off, you know, and I just kept going.' So P4c and P4f have no honest application here. But the phase's underlying job - find the structural gap - was never done in a form that fits an already-consistent prospect, and the obvious gap the transcript hands over (he programmes himself from YouTube, has never had expert eyes on him, and does not know what kettlebell weights to buy) was never named.

P5.evidence: Not run at all - the third consecutive call in this batch with the entire 20-point Consequence Frame absent, and the call where it was most clearly the deciding factor. The rep himself diagnosed the exact problem out loud - 'it just doesn't seem like there's a really like a burning desire' - and P5 is the tool for manufacturing precisely that. Instead of running it he used the absence as grounds to steer the prospect toward a weighted vest. The raw material was sitting there: a 47-year-old who wants to sprint at 67, ski again, and be in a different position from his peers in fifteen years. Not one two-year question, not one 'are you willing to settle for that', no line in the sand.

P6.evidence: The belief question was never asked. The rep offered a binary instead: 'do you feel like it makes sense to just go and do maybe the weighted best and just keep doing what you're doing? Or are you like, no, dude, I definitely would... Where do you want to go from here?' The prospect volunteered an unusually clean commitment in response - 'I guess I would have no problem with committing to doing it. There's no hindrances on whether I would commit to doing it' - which is very close to the yes P6 exists to obtain. It was not banked, not reflected back, and never referenced again once money came up.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted on the flagship and no payment was collected on anything. Even on the downsell the rep declined to take payment on the call and handed off to self-serve: 'you can just go through that yourself. You don't have to give me your card or anything.' Onboarding with Trevor, the agreement email and the welcome/Skool steps were never reachable.

objection_plays.detail: The clearest money trigger in the batch and not one scripted move ran. No isolate ('finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%'), no 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place', no 'most clients pay upfront but for some we break it up', no request for permission to talk openly about finances, and none of the six financial picture questions - cash on hand, monthly surplus, number of credit cards, available credit, used versus available, or investments. This matters more than usual because the prospect had already disclosed he holds a deliberate financial buffer and is near the end of his student loans, which is exactly the situation the financial picture is designed to open up. Instead the rep moved straight to a cheaper product.

Trigger was a pure timing objection - not never, just not yet: 'I might try to circle back around at some point and be like, let's freaking do it, man. I've got this, I've got the money now.' The script exists for this and none of it ran: no 'when does it actually become the right time', no 'things never slow down', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', which lands hard on a 47-year-old whose stated goal is function at 67. The rep instead validated the deferral and added a reason of his own about the prospect's salary.
No think-about-it deferral was raised. The prospect gave a clear decision rather than asking for time.
No spouse or partner consult - he is divorced and the decision was entirely his own.
No fear or doubt objection surfaced; he was confident in his own ability to execute.

Two unscripted triggers, both known gaps. First and most damaging: a cheaper alternative that genuinely worked - five years of free YouTube calisthenics producing a six pack at 10-12% body fat, plus a weighted vest he was already planning to buy. The script assumes the blocker is capacity to pay; here the blocker was that self-direction had a five-year track record of succeeding. The rep not only failed to counter it, he endorsed it: 'I can guarantee you a weighted vest is cheaper... it just probably makes more sense to just continue doing the calisthenics.' Second: a stated demand for a mid-tier option - 'that's my main thing, is it's in the middle of it all' - which has no product behind it and no scripted response.

notes: The structural error is sequencing: the rep named the $200/month Primal University tier at 00:26:18, roughly ten minutes before quoting $6,000, which anchored the prospect against the flagship before he ever heard its price. Combined with a completely absent Consequence Frame on a prospect the rep himself identified as having no burning desire, the call had no path to a close by the time money came up. Coach three things: never name a cheaper internal tier before the flagship price, run P5 hardest when there is no catalyst rather than treating its absence as a disqualifier, and offer the payment plan to a prospect with a temporary and explicitly stated cashflow constraint.
